items.positive_en: What is angioplasty, also called PCI, used to do in coronary arteries narrowed or blocked by plaque?
items.positive_zh: 血管成形术（也叫PCI）用于对被斑块变窄或堵塞的冠状动脉做什么？
items.evidence: Angioplasty is a procedure to improve blood flow in coronary arteries that have become narrow or blocked. Your coronary arteries supply oxygen-rich blood to your heart. If you have coronary artery disease , a sticky material called plaque builds up in your coronary arteries. Plaque is made of cholesterol , calcium, and other substances in your blood. Over time, it can narrow your arteries or fully block them. When this happens, some parts of your heart don't get enough blood. Angioplasty widens the blocked part of your artery so more blood can get through. It is also called percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
items.expected_answer: Angioplasty, or PCI, widens the blocked part of a coronary artery to improve blood flow so more blood can get through.
items.missing_en: What exact percentage of patients have the artery narrow again after angioplasty for coronary artery disease?
items.missing_reason: The summary does not state a precise restenosis percentage; it only says serious problems do not happen very often and may include narrowing of the artery again.

items.positive_en: What is GERD in the context of a hiatal hernia?
items.positive_zh: 在食管裂孔疝的情况下，GERD指的是什么？
items.evidence: When you have a hiatal hernia, it's easier for the acid to come up. This leaking of acid from your stomach into your esophagus is called GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease). GERD may cause symptoms such as : Heartburn Problems swallowing A dry cough Bad breath Nausea and/or vomiting Breathing problems The wearing away of your teeth
items.expected_answer: GERD is leaking of acid from the stomach into the esophagus, and it can happen more easily with a hiatal hernia.
items.missing_en: What exact percentage of people over age 50 have a hiatal hernia?
items.missing_reason: The summary says hiatal hernias are common in people over age 50, but it does not give a precise prevalence percentage.

items.positive_en: What kinds of changes can people with taste and smell disorders experience?
items.positive_zh: 味觉和嗅觉障碍的人可能会经历哪些变化？
items.evidence: People with taste disorders may taste things that aren't there, may not be able to tell the difference in tastes, or can't taste at all. People with smell disorders may lose their sense of smell, or things may smell different. A smell they once enjoyed may now smell bad to them.
items.expected_answer: They may taste things that are not there, be unable to distinguish tastes, lose taste entirely, lose smell, or find that smells change or become unpleasant.
items.missing_en: What exact percentage of older adults lose some ability to taste and smell?
items.missing_reason: The summary says most people lose some ability to taste and smell as they get older, but it does not provide an exact percentage.

items.positive_zh: 低血容量性休克是由什么引起的？
items.evidence: There are several kinds of shock. Hypovolemic shock happens when you lose a lot of blood or fluids. Causes include internal or external bleeding, dehydration, burns, and severe vomiting and/or diarrhea.
items.expected_answer: Hypovolemic shock happens when a person loses a lot of blood or fluids, such as from bleeding, dehydration, burns, or severe vomiting or diarrhea.
items.missing_en: What exact systolic blood pressure threshold defines shock in this summary?
items.missing_reason: The summary says shock causes very low blood pressure and is life-threatening, but it does not state any exact blood pressure threshold.

items.positive_en: What are health screenings designed to find before symptoms appear?
items.positive_zh: 健康筛查旨在在症状出现前发现什么？
items.evidence: Screenings are tests that look for diseases before you have symptoms. Screening tests can find diseases early, when they're easier to treat.
items.expected_answer: Health screenings are tests that look for diseases before symptoms appear and can find diseases early when they are easier to treat.
items.missing_en: What exact percentage improvement in treatment success is achieved when diseases are found early through health screening?
items.missing_reason: The summary says screening can find diseases early when they are easier to treat, but it does not quantify treatment success or provide an effect size.

items.positive_en: How long after infection do Campylobacter infection symptoms usually start?
items.positive_zh: 感染弯曲杆菌后，症状通常多久开始？
items.evidence: Some infected people don't have any symptoms. If you do have symptoms, they start two to five days after you are infected. They usually last about one week, and can include: Diarrhea (which could be bloody) Cramping Abdominal pain Fever Fatigue Nausea and vomiting
items.expected_answer: If symptoms occur, they usually start two to five days after infection.
items.missing_en: What exact percentage of Campylobacter infections lead to Guillain-Barre syndrome?
items.missing_reason: The summary says Guillain-Barre syndrome can occur in rare cases, but it does not state an exact percentage or risk estimate.

items.evidence: Animal diseases that people can catch are called zoonoses. Many diseases affecting humans can be traced to animals or animal products. You can get a disease directly from an animal, or indirectly, through the environment.
items.expected_answer: Zoonoses are animal diseases that people can catch, either directly from animals or indirectly through the environment.
items.missing_en: What exact percentage of human infectious diseases are zoonoses?
items.missing_reason: The summary says many human diseases can be traced to animals or animal products, but it does not provide a precise percentage.

items.positive_en: What areas are included in normal development for children aged 1-3?
items.positive_zh: 1到3岁儿童的正常发育包括哪些方面？
items.evidence: The normal development of children aged 1-3 includes several areas: Gross motor - walking, running, climbing Fine motor - feeding themselves, drawing Sensory - seeing, hearing, tasting, touching, and smelling Language - saying single words, then sentences Social - playing with others, taking turns, doing fantasy play
items.expected_answer: Normal development for children aged 1-3 includes gross motor, fine motor, sensory, language, and social areas.
items.missing_en: What exact percentage of toddlers aged 1-3 have a language delay?
items.missing_reason: The summary notes that toddlers develop at different rates and advises talking to a health care provider about possible delays, but it does not give a percentage for language delay.
